An acquisition-fraction ablation and calibration analysis would strengthen this contribution.

The runtime comparisons are not convincingly matched for posterior accuracy. In Appendix K, the spiking-network comparison uses NLTP -4.72 for NPE versus -4.08 for MF-NPE; the neuron comparison uses -5.87 for NPE versus -5.08 for A-MF-TSNPE, where lower is better. These results demonstrate cost–accuracy tradeoffs but do not establish the stated savings at equivalent quality.

The characterization of when transfer helps is stronger than its evidence. Appendix B studies one OU perturbation family, which cannot establish mutual information as a generally necessary condition or justify the schematic performance bound. Appendix C supplies the standard population NPE loss identity, rather than a transfer-learning convergence or sample-efficiency result.

Reproducibility is weakened by unavailable code and inconsistent experimental descriptions. The spiking-network evaluation uses 10,000 observations in Figure 3 but 262,008 in Appendix D.1; the neuron stimulus also differs between Section 4.2 and Appendix G. These discrepancies matter for verifying the reported results.
